summary: The study investigates the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) using atomic layer deposited MoNx on porous carbon substrates. The MoNx is deposited on carbon cloth (CC) and nitrogen-carbon powder modified carbon cloth (NCCC) using ALD. The as-deposited film shows a nanocrystalline characteristic close to amorphous with a composition of ~Mo2N. The MoNx/NCCC electrode exhibits the highest HER activity due to the high surface area and porosity of the NCCC substrate. Annealing at 400 °C improves both activity and durability, while annealing at 600 °C forms the Mo2C phase, further enhancing activity. The study highlights the importance of porosity and phase changes in the performance of Mo-based catalysts for HER.
evidence: The as-deposited film shows a nanocrystalline characteristic close to amorphous. The film has a composition of ~Mo2N with noticeable oxygen contamination, mainly at the surface. The MoNx/NCCC shows the highest HER activity (overpotential, η of ~236 mV to achieve 10 mA cm-2geo) due to the high surface area and porosity of the NCCC substrate. Annealing at 400 °C improves both the activity and durability of the electrode without significant change in the phase and porosity. Whereas, annealing at an elevated temperature of 600 °C results in the formation of the Mo2C phase that further enhances the activity (η of ~196 mV to achieve 10 mA cm-2geo).
